title: Clarice Lispector's birth chart
metaDescription: Clarice Lispector's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.1° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a square: the Sun and Jupiter within 0.1°, identity wired to expansion. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 18.1° Sagittarius — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Mars. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Sagittarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 28.9° Scorpio, Venus was at 27.5° Capricorn, Mars was at 9.9° Aquarius. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a square within 0.1°. The old texts treat a square as the aspect you feel earliest and thank latest: obstruction first, competence afterwards. Behind it, Mercury sextile Venus at 1.4°, and Mercury square Uranus at 3.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has one entry for this chart. Jupiter in Virgo at 18.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 3 fire, 3 water, 3 earth, 1 air; by modality, 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 2 cardinal. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 18.0°.
